title: Fender Guitar Threats, Drake Lawsuit Ruling, Leak Legal Battles & More Top Music Law News
summary: In this week's Legal Beat newsletter, a looming IP war over guitars, a ruling on Drake's online casino case, a history of song leak lawsuits and much more.
contentText:
THE BIG STORY: Is Fender about to sue the entire guitar industry?

In May, the company started sending cease-and-desist letters to Yamaha, PRS and other guitar makers. They claimed Fender had recently won copyright protection over the iconic design of the Stratocaster electric guitar — and that look-alike “Strat-shaped” guitars would amount to an infringement of those rights.

Related

It turns out Fender’s been trying to get exclusive IP rights to the double cutaway, S-shaped look of the Stratocaster for more than two decades, first with a failed effort to trademark the design in the U.S., and now with a more successful bid for copyright protection in Europe.

But the rest of the industry isn’t taking the threats lying down: “Our client has every right to continue to sell its guitars with Strat-style guitar bodies, whenever and wherever it so chooses,” one opposing lawyer wrote. “Efforts by your client to bully competitors based on misrepresentations and overstatements are anti-competitive.”

For the whole story, go read Rachel Scharf ’s excellent story on the brewing Strat strife . And stay tuned at Billboard to find out if Fender actually files any lawsuits.

Other top stories this week…

-A judge issued a key early ruling in a lawsuit that claims Drake misleadingly endorsed the online casino Stake and used its money to funnel millions of dollars toward artificial streams.

-When Ariana Grande sued over leaks of her unreleased music, she was hardly the first star to do so. As I explained in a historical deep-dive on leak legal battles, BTS , Madonna , Megan Thee Stallion and Kanye West have all lawyered up over a problem that drives artists nuts.

-Sony Music promoted longtime in-house attorney Stephanie Yu to general counsel and executive vp of business and legal affairs after the departure of Julie Swidler .

-A German court ruled Suno broke copyright law by training its AI models on unlicensed songs, one of the first major legal blows to an AI music lab.

-A U.K. judge ordered Amy Winehouse ’s dad to pay over $1 million to two of the late singer’s friends as punishment for an “unjustified and unfounded” lawsuit over merchandise.

– Afroman filed a new lawsuit against one of the Ohio police officers who raided his property, months after the rapper won a high-profile free speech jury verdict against them.

-Ye (formerly Kanye West ) reached a settlement with an ex-staff member who accused him of widespread sexual misconduct.
